correctness.rationale: Every quantifier is over finite positions of one path/cycle with exactly three proper colours. The exact transition identity implies uniform endpoint-pair limits; positive two-step transitions imply exponential saturation of every allowable interior word. Effective Hanf locality reduces any FO named-colour sentence to finitely many endpoint pairs, yielding rational limits and exponential errors. Simultaneous palette relabeling fixes any anonymous sentence, and the orbit action is free because each length-at-least-two endpoint word already uses two distinct colours. The six-member orbit quotient yields exact anonymous numerator divisibility, with converse FO realizability through endpoint equality patterns. Cycle conditioning has probability bounded away from zero, allowing the same saturation argument without endpoints. The binary parity counterexample is exact. Standalone finite enumeration supports but does not replace these universal arguments.

Coupling this with a Markov argument is necessary to obtain limits, and the free diagonal palette action is needed to derive the exact strict loss of denominator 3 in the anonymous three-colour case. No inspected single covering theorem directly supplies the combined conclusion.

originality.rationale: Actual semantic searches of published research records and full-text comparisons with the recent regular-language limit-law paper, earlier FO successor-string characterizations, and colour-forgetting zero–one laws did not reveal a theorem that directly states or entails without additional arguments the strict ternary arithmetic distinction between named and anonymous boundary spectra. value.rationale: The natural distinction between observing three named colours and observing only same-colour equivalence changes the exact set of first-order limiting probabilities, excluding 1/9 yet preserving dense spectra. Both full spectra, effective exponential convergence, an explicit 1/6 anonymous realization and the boundary-free cycle zero–one counterpart are characterized, not merely isolated formula probabilities. This quantifies information loss through symmetry for a canonical locally constrained random language, directly motivated by contemporary work on logical limit laws.
